inspiration.observed_pattern: A MySQL cleanup deletes parent rows selected by a nested grouped subquery whose HAVING comparison equates a filtered child count with a separate scalar count of all children.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Reauthored as a two-project audit purge. A project is deleted only when every ticket is rejected, using an inner grouped candidate query and a correlated scalar total-ticket count; a mixed project remains. The source forum schema, identifiers, rows, and migration data are not copied.

fixture_notes: Project 801 has only rejected tickets and is deleted. Project 802 has one rejected and one approved ticket and remains.
determinism_notes: Project and ticket IDs, states, grouped keys, scalar counts, and final primary-key ordering are fixed; there are no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent schedules.
setup: CREATE TABLE audit_projects (project_id INT PRIMARY KEY, project_name VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL, project_state VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL)
CREATE TABLE audit_tickets (ticket_id INT PRIMARY KEY, project_id INT NOT NULL, ticket_state VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL)

steps.sql: DELETE FROM audit_projects WHERE project_id IN (SELECT doomed.project_id FROM (SELECT p.project_id, COUNT(*) AS rejected_count, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM audit_tickets AS all_tickets WHERE all_tickets.project_id = p.project_id) AS ticket_count FROM audit_projects AS p INNER JOIN audit_tickets AS rejected ON rejected.project_id = p.project_id AND rejected.ticket_state = 'rejected' GROUP BY p.project_id HAVING rejected_count = ticket_count) AS doomed)
SELECT project_id, project_name, project_state FROM audit_projects ORDER BY project_id
SELECT ticket_id, project_id, ticket_state FROM audit_tickets ORDER BY ticket_id
